Name: responsible_item_attribution_benchmark
Title: Which Item Did It? A Seed-Replicated Intervention Benchmark for Attributing Agent Failures to Retrieved Memory Items
Short Hypothesis: A failed ALFWorld episode can be attributed to a specific retrieved memory item only by seed-replicated intervention (re-running the same game with each item removed under 12 seeds); scored against that label, the cheap attributions current systems rely on - the reader's self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain over the failed trajectory, position priors, single-seed leave-one-out - identify the responsible item at least 20 points less often than a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate does on the same episodes, most memory-caused natural failures are not attributable to any single item at all, and duplicating a culprit converts single responsibility into joint responsibility that single-removal labels and single-output methods both miss.
Related Work: Agentic memory benchmarks score end-to-end outcomes only (Evo-Memory arXiv:2511.20857, MemoryArena arXiv:2602.16313, MemoryAgentBench arXiv:2507.05257, MINTEval arXiv:2605.18565, Memora arXiv:2604.20006) and never attribute a failure to an item (G21). CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) and Shapley source attribution (arXiv:2507.04480) intervene per document but in single-shot RAG, without seed replication or cost accounting. Failure attribution for agents exists at the step or agent level: CausalFlow (arXiv:2605.25338, causal responsibility scoring of failure-inducing steps plus counterfactual repair), A2P (arXiv:2509.10401) and ErrorProbe (arXiv:2604.17658) for multi-agent systems, and root-cause benchmarks (arXiv:2509.23735); the retrieved memory item is never the unit. The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) diagnoses adoption of conflicting memory at trajectory level without item-level ground truth or composition arms. Self-explanation faithfulness work (arXiv:2401.07927, arXiv:2307.08678, CC-SHAP arXiv:2311.07466, arXiv:2602.02639) shows self-reports are often unfaithful in classification; nobody has tested self-reported memory use against counterfactual re-runs. Archived retrieved_set_disagreement_gate made a set-level harm claim without item-level ground truth.
Abstract: When a memory-augmented agent fails, which retrieved item, if any, is responsible? No agent-memory benchmark answers this, and the systems that reinforce or demote items on failure use attributions whose accuracy has never been measured. We define item responsibility by intervention: for each failed (game, seed, retrieved set) we re-run the same game with the set intact and with each item removed under 12 seeds (two independent 6-seed blocks), plus an emptied-set arm that says whether memory caused the failure at all; an item is responsible when the one-sided 95% interval of its removal effect excludes zero (analytic power 0.79 at a true effect of 0.5, calibrated on planted culprits). On about 240 natural failures of Qwen3-32B at k=3 and about 225 manufactured failures with a known culprit (a wrong-procedure item planted at position 1 or 3, alone or together with a paraphrased copy of itself), labelling costs 54 re-runs per natural failure. We score attribution methods - position prior, post-episode self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain of the failed action sequence with and without each item, a semantic-overlap heuristic, m-seed leave-one-out from fresh seeds, and exact Shapley - by top-1 accuracy against the label, expressed as a paired gap to a measured ceiling: the accuracy that a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate itself attains on the same episodes. Additivity is tested by pairwise removal with interaction intervals; static-procedure and reader-swap arms are re-measured against the same fresh-seed control so that selection regression cancels. The benchmark releases per-episode responsibility labels with intervals and split-half reliability, the seeds-to-label curve built from seeds disjoint from the label, and the accuracy-versus-cost frontier of the estimators.
Experiments: E0 (free): position prior from the k-sweep logs (which position's items co-occur with failure), and a 500-episode seed-variance pilot at the pre-registered temperature (fixes the failure rate and p(S) variance used below). E1 natural pool: 274 valid games x 2 seeds plus 500 train games x 2 seeds at k=3 (1,548 episodes), expected about 240 failures (15%). Labelling per failure with the failed episode's retrieved set frozen: block A = 6 fresh seeds x (base + 3 single REMOVE arms) = 24 re-runs; block B = 6 further seeds x the same 4 arms = 24; emptied-set arm = 6 seeds at k=0; 54 re-runs per failure, about 13,000 episodes. Label from the pooled 12 seeds: r_i = p(S minus i) - p(S); memory-caused if p(empty) - p(S) >= 0.3 with a one-sided 90% Newcombe interval excluding 0; single-item attributable if the one-sided 95% Newcombe lower bound of max_i r_i exceeds 0 (at m = 12 this needs r_i of about 0.33 or more; analytic power 0.79 at true r = 0.5 and 0.96 at 0.7; per-item false-positive rate 5%); label = argmax_i r_i. Pre-registered extension: if fewer than 80 natural failures are attributable, 500 further train episodes are added (about 75 failures x 54 = 4,050 episodes). E2 manufactured compositions on the same games: planted-only = a wrong-procedure item replaces the natural item at position 1 or 3 (k stays 3), 240 episodes, expected about 60% failures, about 145 failures x block A (24) = 3,500 episodes, the culprit verified by the same rule at 6 seeds; 60 of these failures also get block B (1,440 episodes) so the 12-seed rule is calibrated on known culprits (detection rate, and flag rate on the co-retrieved natural items); two-culprit = the planted item plus a token-matched paraphrase of it replace positions 1 and 3 (set = culprit, culprit-copy, helpful), 120 episodes reusing 120 planted-only games and seeds, expected about 80 failures x (block A 24 + the 4 remaining subsets of 2^3 x 6 seeds = 24) = 3,840 episodes, giving single-removal, pairwise-removal and exact-Shapley responsibility. E3 attribution methods on every failed episode with cost logged: position prior (0 calls); self-report (one extra call, forced choice over the k items plus 'none', two prompts x 3 sampling seeds); teacher-forced confidence gain of the failed action sequence with vs without each item from the served model's prompt log-probabilities (4 scoring passes, no environment steps); semantic overlap between item text and the failing action (0 calls); intervention replicate = block C, 6 fresh seeds x 4 arms on every attributable natural episode (<= 120 x 24 = 2,880 episodes), from which the m-seed LOO curve (m = 1..6, subsampled from C only) and the method ceiling are computed; exact Shapley on 60 attributable natural episodes (4 extra subsets x 6 block-A seeds = 1,440 episodes), which also supplies the pairwise-removal interaction test; pairwise removal on <= 60 memory-caused non-attributable natural failures (3 pairs x 6 seeds = 1,080 episodes) to split them into jointly attributable vs set-level; token-matched REPLACE instead of REMOVE on 60 attributable episodes (3 x 6 = 1,080) as the ground-truth-definition ablation. E4 static-procedure arm: the same <= 120 attributable natural episodes re-run with the type procedure sentence in the prompt, 6 fresh seeds x 4 arms (2,880 episodes); block C is the paired no-sentence control. E5 consumer swap: 100 attributable natural episodes under the second local backbone, 6 seeds x 4 arms (2,400 episodes, served on GPU 1 while GPU 0 runs E4); block C is the paired same-reader control. Totals: about 36,000 episodes (E0 500; pool 1,548; E1 labelling 13,000; E2 9,100; E3 6,500; E4 2,880; E5 2,400), about 30 h at the measured 1,200 episodes/h over two replicas, up to 40,000 episodes / 33 h with the extension; E2 runs on replica 2 while E1 labelling runs on replica 1; block C, E4, E5, Shapley and pairwise cells start once the attributable set is fixed; pre-registration after E0.
Baselines and Ablations: Position prior and random choice as floors; block-C fresh 6-seed LOO as the intervention ceiling on natural episodes and the oracle (planted culprit) as the ceiling in E2; split-half label reliability (block A argmax vs block B argmax); m in {1,...,6} fresh seeds for the accuracy-versus-seeds curve (natural: block C against the 12-seed label; planted: block A against the oracle); REMOVE vs token-matched REPLACE ground truth on 60 episodes; planting at position 1 vs 3; planted-only vs two-culprit compositions for the same planted item on the same games; single vs pairwise removal (interaction intervals) and exact Shapley on the two-culprit arm and on 60 natural episodes; jointly-attributable vs set-level split of non-attributable memory-caused failures; self-report with two elicitation prompts x 3 seeds (own-stability); confidence gain on the failed actions vs on the expert action sequence; abstention scoring on non-attributable episodes for methods with a 'none' option; gross vs static-procedure-net attributability (E4 vs block C); reader swap (E5 vs block C).
Falsifiable Predictions: Definitions: L = 12-seed argmax label on attributable natural episodes; C = accuracy of the fresh 6-seed block-C LOO argmax against L on the same episodes (the intervention-replicate ceiling); PP = position-prior accuracy on the same episodes; every method-versus-ceiling gap is paired over episodes (McNemar; paired bootstrap 90% CI). Validity gate: if C - PP < 20 points the natural label cannot separate methods, and P1-P3 are scored on the E2 planted-only set against the oracle instead and reported as such. P1 Self-report: acc(self-report) <= C - 25 points on attributable natural failures; falsified if acc(self-report) >= C - 5 with the paired 90% CI of the gap excluding 25 (E3 self-report vs block C). Positive control: on E2 planted-only failures self-report must name the planted culprit in >= 60%, otherwise the elicitation is judged broken and P1 is reported as uninterpretable. P2 Confidence gain: acc(confidence gain) <= C - 20 on attributable natural failures; falsified if it is >= C (matches or beats the fresh 6-seed replicate with zero environment steps) with the paired 90% CI of the gap excluding 20 (E3 vs block C); the mechanism favours the method, since a culprit raises the probability of the actions it induced, so this is the prediction most likely to fail. P3 Seeds: single fresh-seed LOO (m = 1 subsampled from block C; an item is named only if it is the unique maximiser of the single-run delta, ties count as abstention; random tie-break reported as secondary) agrees with L in < 65% of attributable natural episodes; falsified if >= 80% with the 95% bootstrap CI excluding 65% (reachable if natural culprits are near-deterministic); secondary, lower-power clause: the smallest m at which the fresh-seed curve comes within 5 points of its m = 6 value is >= 4, falsified if m = 2 already does with the paired 90% CI of acc_6 - acc_2 excluding 10. Nothing in the curve shares seeds with L; the planted set gives the same curve from block A against the oracle. P4 Attributability: among memory-caused natural failures, <= 45% are single-item attributable under the 12-seed rule; falsified if >= 65% with the 95% bootstrap CI excluding 45% (E1). Calibration arm: on the 60 planted-only failures with 12 seeds the rule must detect the planted culprit in >= 80% and flag a co-retrieved natural item in <= 15%; if detection is lower the interval is loosened to one-sided 90% before any prediction is scored (pre-registered); the flag rate on non-memory-caused failures is reported as the empirical false-positive rate; the non-attributable memory-caused remainder is split by pairwise removal into jointly attributable and set-level. P5 Composition: (a) in the two-culprit composition, joint responsibility - each copy's single-removal r < 0.3 while removing both copies passes the attributability rule at 6 seeds (one-sided 90%) - holds in >= 50% of failed episodes; falsified if <= 20% with the 95% CI excluding 50%, i.e. one copy usually suffices to remove (position dominance); the same estimand as a paired contrast: the planted item's single-removal r under planted-only minus under two-culprit on the same games is >= 0.3, falsified if <= 0.1 with the paired 90% CI excluding 0.3 (E2). (b) Additivity on natural attributable failures: the interaction r_ij - r_i - r_j has a 90% interval excluding 0 in >= 30% of (episode, pair) cells; falsified if <= 12% (the nominal rate is 10%) with a cluster bootstrap over episodes (E3 Shapley cell, 60 x 3 pairs). P6 Consumer swap: on 100 attributable natural episodes, the reader-2 6-seed argmax (same rule; 'no item passes' and 'reader 2 succeeds at base' count as disagreement and are reported separately) agrees with L at least 20 points less often than the reader-1 block-C replicate does on the same episodes; falsified if the paired gap is <= 5 points with the 90% CI excluding 20 (E5 vs block C). P7 Static net: on the same <= 120 attributable episodes, the fraction that remain attributable to the same item under the 6-seed rule is >= 25 points lower with the type procedure sentence (E4) than in the paired no-sentence fresh-seed control (block C); falsified if the paired gap is <= 5 points with the 90% CI excluding 25; regression to the mean is identical in both arms, so only the sentence can produce the gap.
Measurement and Noise Control: Label: r_i is a difference of two 12-seed proportions (SE <= 0.20); the rule (one-sided 95% Newcombe lower bound > 0) has analytic power 0.79 at true r = 0.5 and 0.96 at 0.7 with per-item false-positive 5% (about 14% per episode), is calibrated empirically on 60 planted failures at 12 seeds, and its empirical false-positive rate is read off non-memory-caused failures; split-half reliability of the argmax label (block A vs block B) is reported with Spearman-Brown, and the full r_i and p(empty) distributions are released for re-thresholding. Ceiling: every cheap method is compared with the block-C fresh 6-seed LOO on the same episodes, so label noise depresses method and ceiling alike and cannot by itself produce a gap; comparisons are paired (McNemar; paired bootstrap 90% CI over episodes). Sample sizes: 60-110 attributable natural episodes expected, with the pre-registered extension guaranteeing >= 80; at n = 80 a paired accuracy gap has SE about 0.07 (90% CI +/- 11.5 points), so falsifying margins are 15-20 points for P1, P2, P6 and P7, and the 10-point secondary clause of P3 is labelled low-power; P4's proportion over about 100-130 memory-caused failures has a 95% CI of +/- 9 points against a 20-point margin; P5a over about 80 two-culprit failures +/- 11 points against a 30-point margin; P5b uses a cluster bootstrap over episodes for 180 correlated pair cells. Neither the m-seed curve nor the ceiling shares seeds with the label. Sampling temperature is fixed from the E0 pilot and reported; self-report own-stability over 3 seeds x 2 prompts; thresholds, the tie rule, the calibration fallback and the ceiling gate (C - PP >= 20) are pre-registered after E0; multiplicity across seven predictions is handled by reporting all of them; both replicas busy with throughput logged per cell.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both ok); WebSearch not used. (1) mechanism, --recent: 'attribute agent failure to a specific retrieved memory item counterfactual re-run responsible item': CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338 (verified with s2cli paper: step-level causal responsibility scoring and counterfactual repair of failed agent traces; not item-level, no seed-replication or cost report), ErrorProbe arXiv:2604.17658 and A2P arXiv:2509.10401 (agent/step-level attribution in multi-agent systems), root-cause benchmark arXiv:2509.23735, Compliance Trap arXiv:2607.10608 (trajectory-level diagnosis), Phantom Guardrails arXiv:2607.13083 (invented failures). None attributes failures to retrieved memory items with intervention ground truth. (2) home: 'faithfulness of self-explanations counterfactual test which input feature was used language model': arXiv:2401.07927, arXiv:2307.08678, CC-SHAP arXiv:2311.07466, arXiv:2502.18156, arXiv:2602.02639 - self-report faithfulness is tested for classification and reasoning, never for which retrieved item an agent followed. (3) closest named method: 'Shapley attribution retrieved documents RAG LLM calls approximation redundancy evidence utility intervention': only arXiv:2507.04480 (Source Attribution in RAG, PKDD/ECML workshops, 7 citations); single-shot, no stability across calls. (4) 's2cli paper 2605.25338' confirmed the CausalFlow abstract. No preprint provides item-level responsibility labels with seed replication, a seeds-to-label curve, or an accuracy-cost frontier of attribution methods.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Failures at k=3 are about 15% of episodes, and the predicted low attributability makes the natural scoring set small (60-110); the pre-registered extension (+500 train episodes, +4,050 re-runs, about 3 h) keeps it >= 80. If the block-C ceiling is within 20 points of the position prior, the natural label is too noisy to rank methods; P1-P3 are then scored on the planted set and reported as such, and the natural labels are still released with intervals and split-half reliability. Planted culprits are blatant wrong-procedure items, so method accuracies on them bound only the easy end of the difficulty range; the natural set carries the claim. Memory-caused classification uses a 6-seed emptied-set arm (SE about 0.25 for the difference), so weak set-level effects are missed; released p(empty) values allow re-thresholding. The responsibility rule is a design choice, calibrated on planted culprits and released with the full r_i distribution. Negative self-report results depend on elicitation; two prompts and the planted positive control guard this. Confidence gain relies on the served model's prompt log-probabilities; if unavailable, a local forward pass on one GPU replaces it during the E5 phase. Ground truth costs 54 re-runs per failure, so the benchmark is a fixed labelled set rather than a live evaluator. Multiplicity across seven predictions is handled by pre-registration and reporting all. Reader-2 serving must be verified before E5; E5 runs while GPU 0 finishes E4 so no GPU idles.
Addresses gap: G21 (no benchmark attributes a failure to a specific retrieved item in multi-step persistent-memory agents); secondarily G24 (seeds and LLM-call cost of a per-item label, now measured on seeds disjoint from the label) and G25 (composition arm with a duplicated culprit and pairwise-removal additivity test).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Retrieval logs hold per episode the retrieved item ids in rank order, so a nested-k design gives one crude per-position counterfactual for free' - a per-position aggregate cannot name the item responsible for a given failure; this idea produces per-episode item responsibility labels with seed replication and scores attribution methods by their paired gap to what intervention itself achieves, and by cost. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R measures per-evidence utility by intervention in single-shot RAG; cost and variance unreported) - this idea works on multi-step trajectories, measures how many fresh seeds a label needs, and defines memory-caused, single-attributable and jointly-attributable failures as reported quantities. Nearest archived idea: retrieved_set_disagreement_gate claimed harm lives in the set without item-level ground truth; here the item-level ground truth exists and the set-versus-item question is answered by the pairwise-removal split of memory-caused failures.
Changes made: P1, P2: added block C (a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate on every attributable natural episode) as the measured ceiling; both predictions restated as paired gaps to that ceiling with stated margins, a validity gate (C - PP >= 20) and a planted-set fallback, so label noise depresses method and ceiling alike and can no longer produce the result; label raised to 12 seeds. P3: the m-seed curve is now built from block C, disjoint from the seeds that define the 12-seed label, with a pre-registered tie rule; planted curve (block A vs oracle) added as secondary. P4: 12-seed label (two 6-seed blocks) with a CI-based rule of stated analytic power (0.79 at r = 0.5), calibrated empirically on 60 planted failures at 12 seeds with a pre-registered loosening fallback; denominator restricted to memory-caused failures via a new emptied-set arm; remainder split by pairwise removal. P5: the duplicated-helpful composition (whose falsifying branch the construction itself produced) replaced by a two-culprit composition where joint responsibility is an empirical outcome that position dominance falsifies, plus a paired same-game contrast of the planted item's r across compositions; the additivity test is now an interaction interval with a stated nominal false-positive rate instead of Shapley-vs-LOO top-1 disagreement (which noise alone produces); the unmotivated 'methods lose >= 15 points' clause dropped. P6: block C added as the paired same-reader ceiling; statistic is the paired gap. P7: block C is the paired fresh-seed no-sentence control; statistic is the difference of two fresh re-measurements, so selection regression cancels. Budget: REPLACE reduced from every failure to a 60-episode ablation, planted-only 300 to 240 and two-culprit 150 to 120 episodes, Shapley on natural 100 to 60 episodes, confidence gain moved to served prompt log-probabilities; total about 36,000 episodes / 30 h on two replicas, 40,000 / 33 h with the extension. Core claim kept and sharpened: cheap attributions are now predicted to trail the intervention replicate by >= 20 points and most memory-caused failures to be non-attributable, with every falsifying outcome reachable under a named arm.
